note: A research artifact name only. It is not a tenth expert. The nine canonical experts (Prime, Vanguard, Oracle, Nexus, Horizon, Archimedes, Alexandria, Picasso, Forge) are unchanged and Forge's coding/RSI role is not redefined.

hypothesis.statement: An identity-invariant, public-only, deterministic policy over the complete native legal-action menu achieves zero observed catastrophe introductions against both frozen comparators (S0 and Nexus-else-S0) and lowers mean normalized regret by at least 0.02 relative to each, on genuinely fresh, exclusion-aware DEV populations.

thresholds.regretEvidenceRule: point estimate of delta <= -0.02 AND one-sided 95% cluster-bootstrap upper bound of delta < 0, for each comparator separately (delta = policy minus comparator, class-paired)
thresholds.unchanged: the zero-introduction and 0.02 regret thresholds are the originals; nothing is relaxed or re-derived

hypothesis.introduction: runner-design potentialIntroduction({a}, comparator): a is catastrophic in a world where the comparator's action set contains a non-catastrophic action
hypothesis.policyClass: deterministic map from the public decision view to exactly one legal menu action; no abstention; no randomization

permitted: public observation history (complete ObservationPacket sequence, STAGE3H_PUBLIC_DECISION_INFORMATION_V1)
lawfully observable entity attributes and relations (public view only)
frozen S0 top set and frozen Nexus recommendation/rationale codes, each recomputed on whatever view the policy is shown
forbidden: hidden node health or value, cost, risk, resource quantity, relation subtype
native evaluator regret or catastrophe labels, at decision time or as a lookup keyed by public content
recovered or inferred generator seeds, generator random state
privileged native rollouts or any native simulator call at decision time (publicSimulatorCalls must be 0)
offline oracle recommendations or any quantity computed from them
entity ids, action handles, handle order, menu list position, lexical order of any identifier
inputs.comparatorInputRule: S0 and Nexus are re-run on the transformed view. A comparator output enters only as an identity-free projection (membership of an action key in the S0 top set; the key of the Nexus recommendation; rationale codes). A projection that is not stable under relabelling counts against the policy in the invariance test.

actionIdentity.keyV1: type, displacement, target block {kind, rel, flags[critical, objective, hostile, threatened, inService, hub], relationships[[kind, role]] sorted}, params excluding dependent, toX, toY
actionIdentity.keyV2: keyV1 plus, for any action carrying a dependent entity, that dependent's public attribute block {kind, relative position, relative distance, direction, flags incl. resourceFlag, sorted relationships}; plus toX/toY expressed actor-relative
actionIdentity.residualDuplicates: action keys still equal after keyV2 form a symmetric orbit. The policy selects the orbit; evaluator scores catastrophe as worst case over the orbit and regret as uniform expectation (worst case also reported). No lexical order is used to break the tie.
actionIdentity.knownCollisionsResolved: 3 BYPASS groups (idx 6236, 5593, 6198): dependents differ in public kind, relative position, flags and relationships in every group

frames.primary: arm-stressed: classes admitted by the feasibility lane's selection rule (H2, Nexus applicable, N != B, and S0 introducing or both regrets in [40,160]). The rule text is located in the lane's selection source and hashed at I-0; it is not paraphrased here.
frames.secondary: no-harm, unselected: classes the generator emits in the block with no arm-stress filter; zero introductions is required (owner-adjustable to report-only), regret is report-only with no threshold

validation.role: candidate selection, each candidate evaluated once

holdout.twinDraws: 40 standard plus 120 extra from an independently salted stream plus up to 64 corner settings of hiddenSupport; used once

populations.disjointness: pairwise disjoint seed blocks, disjoint base-world lineages, disjoint public-class digests (coarse digest), and disjoint from the 341 inspected classes and from every spent source
populations.inspectedClasses: the 341 classes (DEV288 3, block 951 153, block 952 185) may serve only as development fixtures/smoke tests. They are excluded from training, validation and holdout statistics. 'FRESH_*' labels on them are legacy and wrong; they are spent.
populations.originFamilyCap: no topology x resource x objective family may exceed 5% of the classes of a population
populations.familyDisjointStressHoldout: secondary, non-gating; evaluable only if at least 20 origin families are absent from exploration and validation

exclusion.layer1: stage3h-wider-action-feasibility-v1/exclusion/strict-index.mjs: loadStrictIndex, preflightNamespace({base,count}), preflightWorlds(hashes); fail-closed; replaces the closure validateSeedRange endpoint-only check
exclusion.layer2: public-class digest (PCD), built at I-2: relabel-invariant (equivalent views always give equal digests; collisions between non-equivalent views are accepted and over-exclude), D4-canonical (minimum over the 8 transforms), menu-order-canonical (menu sorted by keyV2, handles removed), digest fields stripped. Exclusion uses the coarse form (menu key multiset, comparator projections, public aggregates; sequence and timestamps dropped).
exclusion.spentSourceCoverage: regenerate-and-digest only DEV and diagnostic sources whose public views are already unsealed; every sealed or otherwise non-regenerable source is excluded at whole-seed-block level and is never regenerated. V4 sealed worlds and their labels are never used. Coverage percentage is reported.
exclusion.mutual: each H-W1 population registers its PCDs before the next population is generated

claims.C1: observed zero introductions on finite DEV data (counts only)
claims.C2: one-sided 95% upper bound on the class-level catastrophe-introduction rate: 1 - 0.05^(1/n) at zero events; the cluster-level bound over origin families is reported beside it and the larger is the headline
claims.C3: universal guarantee over admissible native states: NOT CLAIMED; requires a separate proof over the admissible hidden-state domain
claims.C4: generalization to the seeded generator population: limited to the stated frame, generator version, rule hash and seed namespace

invariance.relabel: O-2R.1 identityViewTwinV2 plus 5 random relabellings per class, comparators recomputed; chosen key must be equal
invariance.menuOrder: 5 random permutations plus reverse; chosen key equal
invariance.d4: 7 non-identity transforms; chosen key must be the transformed key; claimed only if evaluator labels are first shown D4-equivariant on a sample (I-0)
invariance.publicOnly: twins of a class must give bit-identical output; policy runs with hidden accessors made to throw; negative-control policies (handle-order dependent, hidden-state dependent) must be detected

evaluation.legality: chosen action is in the native menu and accepted by the native legality check; zero illegal selections; no abstention
evaluation.catastrophe: per world and per class, vs S0 and vs Nexus-else-S0, over base plus twins; base-world-only count reported separately; both must be zero
evaluation.regret: class-level nreg is the equal-weight mean over the twin family (as in the feasibility lane); base-world-only and worst-case reported; delta vs each comparator, class-paired, cluster bootstrap over origin families (10000 resamples, seeded)
evaluation.reproducibility: deterministic seeds derived by hash from registered labels; single-threaded deterministic aggregation; node version recorded; no wall clock in any decision; write-once evidence (writeExclusive); two independent runs must give byte-identical per-class decisions and aggregate digests; freeze record binds policy artifact hash, code hashes, contract hash, population plan hash

invalidateRun: forbidden input detected statically or dynamically
any access to sealed worlds or V4 labels
custody audit not passing at the start of a phase
rejectCandidate: regret evidence rule unmet on validation
refuteOnHoldout: any introduction vs either comparator on the frozen policy (final; holdout spent)
notSupported: population below minimum after the allocated namespace is exhausted (INSUFFICIENT_POPULATION; the rule and minimum n are not relaxed)
